In a recent press conference, the Prime Minister has announced plans to make farmers replace Jute production with Hemp. Jute, a cash crop used chiefly in making rope, is one of the major exports of Bangladesh. If this move is successful, Bangladesh could potentially become the leading exporter of Hemp products. The Prime Minister gave a simple statement:

"If we are to compete with the westerners, we must adopt new ways of thinking. Jute is no longer a viable product to produce in a modern economy."

The government not only plans to make hemp rope, they also plan to use the prosperous clothing industry to make a new line of clothes. Through state subsidies, they are also planning to make hemp products cheaper than anything offered from the competition. The money, they say, will come from Marijuana. Since Cannabis is essentially legal in Bangladesh, the government plans to make a hefty profit on both exports and taxes. Currently, they're willing to make trade deals with any nation that has legalized the popular drug. The plans will begin by the end of the Monsoon Season this September.
